title: Boyhood homemade-instrument groups and fence music
summary: Asked about unusual groups, he recalls Slow Drag's homemade bass, violinists Lucian and Willis St. Diego, Freddie Gould, and boys beating wires on a fence.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Is there anything else about your life that you'd like to tell? We've only got a couple more minutes here on the tape and if there's anything else that you could tell I think we can finish up on this reel if you've got the work then. I know you've got other things on your mind too. Anything about especially when you were young the kind of music you heard when you were a boy? Were there any other little groups around you know on unusual instruments like large board bands or tubbers or anything?

Oh yeah. Drag had a homemade bass. A fun one they called Tone Meters. That's right. I've heard you told us a little bit about that. They used to have another fellow called Lucian who played the violin. And another fellow, he was some kind of a St. Avril boy who played piano, he used to play the violin. He was well at St. Avril. Oh yeah I heard it again, I never got there.

And violin, guitar, a fellow called Freddie Gould, I believe he was living somewhere in Alton town. He was a wonderful old time guitar picker. And Freddie Gould and slow drag, Lucian on violin. Willis St. Diego played the violin. And Freddie Gould played the guitar.
